chunks: Ali ibn Isma'il from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
The waiting period ('iddah) of a female slave whose husband dies is two months and five days, and the waiting period of the divorced woman who does not menstruate is one month and a half.
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a female slave whose husband dies or a divorced woman who does not menstruate?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar delineates the specific 'iddah periods for a female slave whose husband dies (two months and five days) and a divorced woman who is post-menstruation (one and a half months), reflecting the juristic principle that their waiting periods are half that of free women. It highlights the nuanced application of Quranic rulings to different social statuses within the early Shia legal tradition.
